 Taylor Ardrey USA TODAY Oct. 23, 2026, 11:33 a.m. ET Hear this story Jaguar Land Rover , the parent company of the those two vaunted brands, is recalling more than 93,000 vehicles due to a defect that could reduce driver visibility and increase the risk of a crash.
 According to a recall notice posted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, certain vehicles manufactured by Jaguar Land Rover North America, LLC are being recalled due to water not properly draining from the rearview cameras, citing "insufficient drain holes."
 "A blurred image or lack of display of the rearview camera image may result in the driver being unaware of objects or pedestrians," the safety recall report says.
 Here's what we know about the model of vehicle that's included the recall and what car owners should do next.
 What model is included in the Jaguar Land Rover recall?
 According to the NHTSA, 93,997 vehicles are potentially affected. The model included in the recall is:
 2022-2026 Land Rover Range Rover
 The recall number is D171.
 What should car owners do?
 Car owners are advised to take their vehicles to the dealership for an inspection and, if necessary, to have their rearview camera replaced at no charge, the NHTSA said. Additionally, drain holes will be drilled in the underside of the tailgate trim.
 Notification letters will be sent out on Dec. 11. Another will be mailed when a final remedy is available.
 Jaguar Land Rover can be reached at 800-637-6837.
